chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the child who steals. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He is excused from it once and twice, and he is rebuked in the third. So if he repeats, the tips of his fingers are cut. So if he repeats, lower than that is cut.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on punishing a child for theft?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a graduated penal procedure for juvenile theft, moving from initial exemption to corporal punishment, reflecting the Shia principle of balancing mercy with corrective discipline for those not yet fully bound by Hadd obligations. This progression underscores the juristic distinction between the fixed Hadd penalty for adults and the discretionary (Ta'zir) punishment applied to children, emphasizing rehabilitation over immediate retribution.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd, from Yunus, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the child who steals. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He would be excused from it once, and twice, and he would be rebuked during the third. So if he repeats, a bit of his finger would be cut. So if he repeats, lower than that would be cut’.
